precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil.
precepts.point: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.
precepts.why: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” That answers Job's question: “Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?” Because the sentence is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil. They live and grow old in it because the judgment has not yet fallen. This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.

precepts.text: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times and his days be prolonged, yet it shall be well with them that fear God.
precepts.point: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.
precepts.why: “Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him”. The wicked do live, become old, and are mighty in power; a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged. But that is not the end of it: yet it shall be well with them that fear God. The prolonged days of the wicked are no proof that they are right; it is well with them that fear before him.

precepts.text: Their inward thought is that their houses shall continue forever, and they call their lands after their own name.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.
precepts.why:
“Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.” That is the mind of the wicked in Job 21: “Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes. Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.” This is why they think the way they do, because no rod falls on them, so they think their houses continue forever and call their lands after their own name.

This is going twofold, dealing with the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau. This passage is the pride of Esau.

precepts.text: Nevertheless man being in honor abideth not, so the honor does not last.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.
precepts.why: “Nevertheless man being in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish.” The honor does not last. Their seed is established in their sight, their houses are safe from fear, and no rod of God is upon them, so they think the way they do. Nevertheless, man in honor abideth not. This is the pride of Esau, and it goes twofold, for the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau; neither one's honor abides.

precepts.text: When Israel is wicked, curses fall as a nation: the ox slain before your eyes, the ass taken away, the seed given to the enemy with none to rescue.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.
precepts.why:
“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.” When Israel is wicked, curses fall as a nation: the ox slain before your eyes, the ass taken away, the seed given to the enemy with none to rescue.

That is the opposite of what Job sees in the wicked: “Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.” They are even prosperous in their animals, while the rod of God is not upon them. This is going twofold, dealing with the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau, and this passage is the pride of Esau; Israel's wickedness brings the curse on its cattle, while Esau's beasts fail not.

precepts.text: They that dwell on the earth rejoice, make merry, and send gifts one to another, mocking the two prophets, the northern and southern kingdom of Israel.
precepts.point: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave. The wealth is real, but the end comes suddenly.
precepts.why:
“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.” They rejoice, make merry, and send gifts one to another, mocking the two prophets, the northern and southern kingdom of Israel.

That is the wicked of Job 21: “They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance. They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.” This is the wicked holiday, Christmas: they make merry, make songs, and send gifts. They spend their days in wealth, and the wealth is real, but “in a moment go down to the grave.” The end comes suddenly.

precepts.text: Ho, ho, come forth and flee from the land of the north. Santa Claus mocks you by quoting this while holding you in captivity; they hide the truth in your face to see how dumbed down we are.
precepts.point: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave. The wealth is real, but the end comes suddenly.
precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Santa Claus mocks you by quoting this while holding you in captivity. They hide the truth in your face to see how dumbed down we are.

That is the merry-making of Job 21, the wicked holiday, Christmas: their children dance, they take the timbrel and harp and rejoice at the sound of the organ, they make songs and send gifts. The Lord says come forth and flee from the land of the north, and they turn it into “Ho, ho” over a people spread abroad as the four winds of the heaven. They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

precepts.text: The Most High knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to reserve the unjust to the day of judgment to be punished.
precepts.point: Have you not asked them that go by the way, and do you not know their tokens? The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
precepts.why:
“The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished”. That is the token Job says they should know: “the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.”

Job knows their thoughts and the devices they wrongfully imagine against him when they ask where the house of the prince is and where the dwelling places of the wicked are. Ask them that go by the way. The Most High knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to reserve the unjust to the day of judgment to be punished; the wicked's prosperity is only a reservation until the day of wrath.

precepts.text: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
precepts.point: Have you not asked them that go by the way, and do you not know their tokens? The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
precepts.why: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” The wicked that is reserved to the day of destruction has a name. The Most High hated Esau, and that is why the dwelling places of the wicked stand for now: he is being reserved, to be brought forth to the day of wrath.

precepts.text: For this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee; Esau raised up to be destroyed like Pharaoh.
precepts.point: Have you not asked them that go by the way, and do you not know their tokens? The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
precepts.why:
“For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” Esau was raised up to be destroyed like Pharaoh. That is why the wicked has a house and a dwelling place at all: he was raised up for this same purpose, that the Most High might show his power in him.

So the wicked is “reserved to the day of destruction” and “brought forth to the day of wrath.” His rising was the setup for the showing of God's power, and his name declared throughout all the earth.

precepts.text: God endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction; some were made just to be destroyed.
precepts.point: Have you not asked them that go by the way, and do you not know their tokens? The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
precepts.why:
“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. Some were made just to be destroyed. God endures the vessels of wrath with much long-suffering, and that long-suffering is what looks like the prosperity of the wicked.

That is the answer to “Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?” The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction, endured for now, and shall be brought forth to the day of wrath. Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; Esau was raised up like Pharaoh, a vessel of wrath fitted to destruction.

points: Job tells his friends to hear his speech and let this be their consolation. Suffer me that I may speak, and after I have spoken, mock on. Let Job speak, then see if you have anything to say, or mock him.
Job asks a direct question: is my complaint to man? If it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled? His complaint is not against men, so his trouble is justified.
Mark me and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth. When Job remembers, he is afraid, and trembling takes hold on his flesh.
Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.

Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes. Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them. This is why they think the way they do, because no rod falls on them.
Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.

They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance. They take the timbrel and harp and rejoice at the sound of the organ. This is the wicked holiday, Christmas: they make merry, make songs, and send gifts.
They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave. The wealth is real, but the end comes suddenly.
Therefore they say unto God, depart from us, for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways. This is why the fool has said in his heart there is no God, and why they call themselves atheists.
What is the Almighty that we should serve him, and what profit shall we have if we pray unto him? Lo, their good is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from Job.

How oft is the candle of the wicked put out? How oft cometh their destruction upon them? God distributeth sorrows in his anger. They are as stubble before the wind and as chaff that the storm carries away.

God layeth up his iniquity for his children; he rewardeth him, and he shall know it. His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty. They are going to drink from the wrath of God.
For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst? The prosperity means nothing once his time is cut short.

Shall any teach God knowledge, seeing he judgeth those that are high? One dies in his full strength, wholly at ease and quiet, his breasts full of milk and his bones moistened with marrow, in his prime.
Another dies in the bitterness of his soul and never eateth with pleasure, poor and needy. They shall lie down alike in the dust, from the best to the worst, and the worms shall cover them.
Job says he knows their thoughts and the devices which they wrongfully imagine against him. They ask, where is the house of the prince, and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
Have you not asked them that go by the way, and do you not know their tokens? The wicked is reserved to the day of destruction; they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.

Who shall declare his way to his face, and who shall repay him what he hath done? He is brought to the grave and remains in the tomb, and every man draws after him as there are innumerable before him.
Job says their counsel comforts him in vain, seeing in their answers there remaineth falsehood. When you read the whole book, God lets them know that Job was right.
